title: Fail well: retries, breakers, hedges and failover
brief: Calls to the model fail in different ways: a blip, an exhausted quota, a slow tail, a dead region. Each deserves a different response, and the wrong one makes things worse. How critical the call is, whether it is cheap to repeat and how long recovery may take are all open.

blocks.text: Match the pattern to the failure

blocks.title: Pick the resilience pattern
blocks.prompt: Flip the failure type, the nature of the call and how critical it is.

values.label: Degradable, a reduced answer is fine

blip.why: Honor Retry-After, add jitter and cap attempts and total time.

quota.why: Retrying quota or billing errors never succeeds, so do not.

region.why: Retries pile onto a dead region.

tail.why: Retries fire after a failure, not after slowness.

cheap.why: A repeat costs little and is safe.

costly.why: Repeats are expensive, and stateful calls may not be safe to repeat.

critical.why: Often enough to save the request.

soft.why: A fallback may be a better use of the time.

blip.why: Trips after repeated failures and spreads load.

quota.why: A pool shifts traffic to a deployment with headroom.

region.why: Priority groups route to a healthy region while the breaker trips the bad one.

tail.why: A breaker reacts to failures, not to slowness.

costly.why: Stateful APIs need session affinity behind a pool.

critical.why: Keeps a path to a working backend.

quota.why: A second region brings its own quota.

region.why: The only pattern that survives a regional outage, and you build it yourself.

cheap.why: Works, but the standby is a fixed cost.

costly.why: State and prompt caches are per region, so a failover starts cold.

critical.why: Recovery targets range from minutes to hours by tier.

soft.why: A standby costs more than degradation for non-critical work.

blip.why: A duplicate does not help a rejected request.

quota.why: Duplicates add load to an exhausted quota.

region.why: Only helps if the duplicate can reach another region.

tail.why: Cut p99.9 from 1,800 ms to 74 ms for about 2% more requests in the BigTable benchmark.

cheap.why: Cheap and idempotent is the safe case for duplicates.

costly.why: A duplicate long generation doubles real spend.

critical.why: Trims the tail on critical paths.

quota.why: Smaller model, shorter output, cached answer, queue or shed.

region.why: Keeps the core flow alive on reduced capacity.

tail.why: Cutting work fits the time budget.

costly.why: A cheaper fallback beats paying twice.

critical.why: A degraded answer may break the guarantee.

soft.why: The product decision is already made.

blocks.takeaway: Name the failure first. Retries fix blips, degradation fixes sustained quota pressure, a second region fixes a regional outage and hedging fixes only the tail.

blocks.caption: Retry and hedging rules from the sources
head: Technique
Rule
Source
rows: Treat it as a minimum and add a small random delay
Without a header, use exponential backoff with jitter. Capped backoff alone leaves retry clusters, and jitter spreads them and cuts total calls
Count SDK retries so nested loops do not multiply traffic
After about the p95 delay send a duplicate and take the first reply. In a Google BigTable benchmark, p99.9 for 1,000 keys fell from 1,800 ms to 74 ms for about 2% extra requests

blocks.title: What a circuit breaker does
blocks.alt: State diagram. The breaker starts closed. When the failure count is reached in the interval it moves to open. After the trip duration, or the accepted Retry-After value, it returns to closed.

blocks.caption: In APIM a tripped backend makes the gateway return 503 for traffic that would have gone to it [[r4]].

blocks.title: A backend circuit breaker rule (illustrative)
blocks.caption: A backend has one `circuitBreaker` rule with `failureCondition`, `tripDuration` and `acceptRetryAfter`. Rules are approximate across gateway instances and are not in the Consumption tier. For Azure OpenAI backends accept `Retry-After`, because it can be large, for example a day. Pools hold up to 30 backends with round-robin (default), weighted or priority balancing, and lower priority groups are used only when higher ones are tripped [[r4]].
Regional recovery tiers. Foundry does not fail over automatically, so you build two resources in two regions with two project connections [[r15]]

blocks.title: Failure modes of the failure handling

items.symptom: A short blip becomes a long outage
items.cause: A retry storm: SDK, application and gateway each retry, so three layers with three retries each send up to 4 x 4 x 4 = 64 attempts per request
items.fix: Keep one retry layer, cap attempts and total time, add jitter and a breaker. Detect with requests per unique task id

items.symptom: A breaker never opens for one failing gateway instance
items.cause: Rules are approximate because gateway instances do not synchronize
items.fix: Treat it as best effort and watch backend failure rates centrally

items.symptom: Clients see 503 and blame the model
items.cause: A tripped breaker makes the gateway itself return 503
items.fix: Tag gateway-originated errors in logs and traces and alert on breaker-open time

items.symptom: Failover works on paper and fails in the incident
items.cause: The second region has no quota, deployment or model version, and Foundry does not fail over for you
items.fix: Create both deployments in advance, add Service Health alerts and availability tests, and rehearse. Front Door with one APIM per region can route around a dead region

items.symptom: Cost and p95 TTFT jump after failover
items.cause: Prompt caches are not shared across regions, so the standby starts cold
items.fix: Prewarm where possible and budget for the cold start

items.symptom: Stateful conversations break when traffic moves
items.cause: Stateful APIs such as Responses need session affinity behind a backend pool
items.fix: Enable session awareness on the pool, or keep conversation state outside the model API

quiz.q: Put the handling of a failed model call in order, following OpenAI's retry guidance.
items: Classify the error: do not retry quota or billing errors
Wait at least the Retry-After value, otherwise use exponential backoff
Add a small random jitter to the delay
Stop at the attempt cap or the total time budget
Fall back or degrade instead of retrying again
quiz.explain: Classification comes first because some errors can never succeed. The wait honors the server's hint as a minimum. Jitter prevents synchronized retries. Caps bound the cost, and a fallback is the exit when the budget runs out.

quiz.q: An SDK, an application wrapper and a gateway each make one attempt plus 3 retries. When the backend keeps failing, how many calls can reach the backend for one user request?
quiz.explain: Each layer makes 4 attempts per attempt of the layer above, so 4 x 4 x 4 = 64. This is why OpenAI advises counting SDK retries, and why one retry layer with a cap and jitter is the safer design.

quiz.q: Which hedging policy fits an LLM workload best?
options: Hedge every call after 50 ms to cut the median, since duplicates cost less than slow answers
Hedge long streaming generations, because they have the worst tails and duplicates add little load
Never hedge LLM calls, because a duplicate can only make the tail worse under load
Hedge cheap idempotent calls after about the p95 delay, cap the extra spend and cancel the loser
quiz.explain: Hedging works when the duplicate is cheap and safe, fires after about the p95 delay and has a spend cap. Hedging at 50 ms doubles load without helping the tail. Duplicating long generations doubles the real cost. Never hedging ignores the large p99.9 gains reported for cheap calls.

takeaways: Name the failure, then pick the pattern. Retries for blips, degradation for quota pressure, a second region for outages, hedging for tails
Never retry quota or billing errors, and keep to one retry layer with jitter and caps
A tripped APIM breaker returns 503 from the gateway, so label gateway errors in your traces
Foundry does not fail over for you. Build, test and rehearse the second region
Failover starts with a cold prompt cache and may lack quota, so plan for cost and latency
